overview: The RF NIC Card houses a sub-GHz RF module with an external antenna and an interface connector for establishing communication with smart meters. It promptly monitors energy meters, ensuring utilities industry-standard energy efficiency, ultra-fast wake-up times, a scalable power amplifier and an integrated balun.

The module is built on a high-performance 32-bit 40 MHz ARM Cortex-M4 CPU with 1024 KB flash and 128 KB RAM, running from a 38.4 MHz crystal. It transmits at +20 dBm in the 865–867 MHz band with −98 dBm receive sensitivity and an 800 m line-of-sight range.

It sits in the same AMR ecosystem as the gas and water AMR devices — meter (magnetic / inductive / RS485) to AMR to gateway/DCU to network server or IoT middleware and the end-user application — and operates from −20 °C to +65 °C.
